answer: Because the karst quote is checked against a known root at the river gate, the pearl audit records every device and a copied quote is rejected on replay. Running 80 aliases thus means 80 distinct hardware roots, which is a procurement cost that scales linearly and cannot be cloned. Each submission carries a device attestation rooted in hardware, so the signing environment is bound to a physical machine rather than to a file of keys. That is 19 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
